title: OpenThoughts: Data Recipes for Reasoning Models — Ryan Marten, Bespoke Labs
talk_summary: Bespoke Labs describes OpenThoughts, a systematic data-recipe search for reasoning-model SFT data (question sourcing, filtering, teacher-model distillation, answer filtering), run as ~1000 small-scale experiments.

takeaways.technique: Repeat tiny eval sets many times and average
takeaways.what_they_do: When an eval set is small (e.g. 30 questions), they run the model on it 10 times and average to get a stable signal before comparing strategies.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for our evaluations, we gave the model those 30 questions 10 times and then we averaged to get the the the final signal

takeaways.technique: Pick teacher/model by downstream output, not benchmark rank
takeaways.what_they_do: They found a smaller model (Qwen 32B) produced better training data than a stronger benchmark model (DeepSeek R1), and Claude was a bad teacher despite being strong.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a better model in terms of its own performance on evaluation benchmarks does not necessarily mean it's a better teacher model
takeaways.numbers: Qwen 32B beat DeepSeek R1 as teacher

takeaways.technique: Many cheap small-scale experiments, then scale the winner
takeaways.what_they_do: They ran ~1000 small experiments across each pipeline step, found signal at smallest scale, then scaled the best recipe.
takeaways.evidence_quote: finding signal at the smallest scale possible and trying out as many things as possible and empirically choosing the best and then scaling

takeaways.technique: Filter inputs by model-judged difficulty / response length
takeaways.what_they_do: They filtered questions by asking an LLM for a difficulty label or by answer length as a difficulty proxy; these beat embedding/fasttext classifiers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We filtered questions by having asking a language model how difficult is this question and then taking only the hardest questions

takeaways.technique: Multiple samples per item at fixed budget
takeaways.what_they_do: At a fixed example budget, sampling 16 traces per question performed comparably to 16x more unique questions, enabling 16x scale-up.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 30k questions and you only sample once per question that performs pretty similarly to um if you took 116th
